info.title: Backpack Exchange API
info.description:
# Introduction Welcome to the Backpack Exchange API. This API is for programmatic trade execution. Endpoints require requests to be signed with an ED25519 keypair for authentication, unless documented otherwise. To get started, create an API key in the [API Keys section of your account settings](https://backpack.exchange/settings/api-keys) on the exchange. The API is hosted at `https://api.backpack.exchange/` and the WS API is hosted at `wss://ws.backpack.exchange/`. # Authentication ## Signing requests Signed requests are required for any API calls that mutate state. Additionally, some read only requests can be performed by signing or via session authentication. Signed requests require the following additional headers: - `X-Timestamp` - Unix time in milliseconds that the request was sent. - `X-Window` - Time window in milliseconds that the request is valid for, default is `5000` and maximum is `60000`. - `X-API-Key` - Base64 encoded verifying key of the ED25519 keypair. - `X-Signature` - Base64 encoded signature generated according to the instructions below. ### Generate ED25519 Keys You can generate a private/public ED25519 keypair using this Python one-liner: ```python python3 -c "from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ed25519; import base64; key = ed25519.Ed25519PrivateKey.generate(); seed = key.private_bytes_raw(); pub = key.public_key().public_bytes_raw(); print(f'Seed: {base64.b64encode(seed).decode()}\nPublic Key: {base64.b64encode(pub).decode()}')" ``` This will output your base64-encoded private key (seed) and public key that can be used for API authentication. ### Signature Generation To generate a signature perform the following: 1) The key/values of the request body or query parameters should be ordered alphabetically and then turned into query string format. 2) Append the header values for the timestamp and receive window to the above generated string in the format `×tamp=&window=`. If no `X-Window` header is passed the default value of `5000` still needs to be added to the signing string. Each request also has an instruction type, valid instructions are: ``` accountQuery accountUpdate balanceQuery borrowLendExecute borrowHistoryQueryAll borrowLendPositionQuery borrowPositionHistoryQueryAll collateralQuery convertDust depositAddressQuery depositQueryAll dustHistoryQueryAll fillHistoryQueryAll fundingHistoryQueryAll interestHistoryQueryAll maxBorrowQuantity maxOrderQuantity maxWithdrawalQuantity orderCancel orderCancelAll orderExecute orderHistoryQueryAll orderQuery orderQueryAll positionHistoryQueryAll positionQuery quoteAccept quoteFillHistoryQueryAll quoteHistoryQueryAll quoteSubmit rfqCancel rfqFillHistoryQueryAll rfqHistoryQueryAll rfqQuery rfqRefresh rfqSubmit settlementHistoryQueryAll strategyCancel strategyCancelAll strategyCreate strategyHistoryQueryAll strategyQuery strategyQueryAll withdraw withdrawalQueryAll ``` The correct instruction type should be prefixed to the signing string. The instruction types for each request are documented alongside the request. For example, an API request to cancel an order with the following body: ```json { "orderId": 28 "symbol": "BTC_USDT", } ``` Would require the following to be signed: ```text instruction=orderCancel&orderId=28&symbol=BTC_USDT×tamp=1614550000000&window=5000 ``` Regarding batch order execution (`POST /orders`), for each order in the batch, the order parameters should be ordered alphabetically and then turned into query string format. The orderExecute instruction should then be prefixed to that string. The query strings for the orders should be concatenated with `&` and the timestamp and window appended at the end. For example, an API request for an order execution batch with the following body: ```json [ { "symbol": "SOL_USDC_PERP", "side": "Bid", "orderType": "Limit", "price": "141", "quantity": "12" }, { "symbol": "SOL_USDC_PERP", "side": "Bid", "orderType": "Limit", "price": "140", "quantity": "11" } ] ``` Would require the following to be signed: ```text instruction=orderExecute&orderType=Limit&price=141&quantity=12&side=Bid&symbol=SOL_USDC_PERP&instruction=orderExecute&orderType=Limit&price=140&quantity=11&side=Bid&symbol=SOL_USDC_PERP×tamp=1750793021519&window=5000 ``` If the API endpoint requires query parameters instead of a request body, the same procedure should be used on the query parameters. If the API endpoint does not have a request body or query parameters, only the timestamp and receive window need to be signed. This message should be signed using the private key of the ED25519 keypair that corresponds to the public key in the `X-API-Key` header. The signature should then be base64 encoded and submitted in the `X-Signature` header.

--- # RFQ Lifecycle The sequence below shows the lifecycle of an RFQ, including the deferred settlement branch used by the exchange broker on stock markets. Event names are those emitted on the `account.rfqUpdate` WebSocket stream. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Requester participant Engine participant Maker Requester->>Engine: POST /rfq (rfqSubmit) Engine-->>Requester: rfqAccepted Engine-->>Maker: rfqActive (broadcast) Maker->>Engine: POST /rfq/quote (quoteSubmit) Note over Engine: Quotes accepted until the submission time (w) Engine-->>Requester: rfqCandidate (new best quote) Requester->>Engine: POST /rfq/accept (quoteAccept) alt Standard quote - immediate settlement Engine-->>Requester: rfqFilled Engine-->>Maker: rfqFilled else Deferred settlement quote (exchange broker, stock markets) Engine-->>Requester: rfqAcceptedBinding (funds locked) Engine-->>Maker: rfqAcceptedBinding Maker->>Engine: quoteSettle (broker only) Engine-->>Requester: rfqFilled (quoted or improved price) Engine-->>Maker: rfqFilled end ``` If no quote is accepted by the expiry time (`W`), the RFQ expires. An open RFQ can be cancelled (`rfqCancel`), or refreshed (`rfqRefresh`), which cancels its existing quotes and restarts the submission and expiry windows. A binding accepted RFQ that is not settled within the settlement window is cancelled by the system and the locked funds are released.

--- # Stock Trading Tokenized stocks trade through the RFQ (Request For Quote) flow while the security's market sessions are open, with quotes provided by the exchange broker. Certain listed stocks also have a spot order book market; outside of market hours, trading in these flows through the spot order book using the standard order endpoints, like any other spot market. Stocks without a spot order book market trade exclusively through the RFQ flow. ## Discovering stock markets - `GET /api/v1/securities` lists the tradable securities, the market sessions each security trades in, and its quantity constraints per session. - RFQ market symbols have the form `_USDC_RFQ`, for example `AAPL.US_USDC_RFQ`. They are not returned by `GET /api/v1/markets`. - Spot order book markets for listed stocks appear in the default `GET /api/v1/markets` response with the `rwaMarketType` field set to `STOCK`, for example `MU.US_USDC`. - `GET /api/v1/stockSessions` and `GET /api/v1/stockHolidays` describe session hours, market closures and shortened trading days. - `GET /api/v1/ticker`, `GET /api/v1/tickers` and `GET /api/v1/klines` support stock market symbols. All three additionally accept `source=External` to return external market data. ## Trading flow While the security's market sessions are open, trading uses the RFQ flow (see the RFQ Lifecycle section for the full event sequence): 1. Submit an RFQ with `POST /api/v1/rfq`, specifying the stock RFQ market symbol, `side`, and `quantity` (in the security). `quoteQuantity` is not currently supported for stock RFQs — such requests receive no quotes and expire. 2. Quotes are provided by the exchange broker. Monitor them on the `account.rfqUpdate` WebSocket stream or by polling `GET /api/v1/rfqs`. 3. Accept a quote with `POST /api/v1/rfq/accept`. Alternatively, submit the RFQ with `executionMode=Immediate` and a `price` — the first quote at or better than that price is accepted automatically. Outside of market hours, stocks with a spot order book market trade using the standard order endpoints (e.g. `POST /api/v1/order`) on the spot market symbol. ## Deferred settlement Quotes provided by the exchange broker on stock markets use deferred settlement. This changes the post-acceptance lifecycle compared to a regular RFQ: - Accepting the quote is binding. The trade is confirmed at the quoted price and the funds required to pay for it are locked, along with any fee payable in the same asset (a fee payable in a different asset is deducted from the proceeds at settlement). An `rfqAcceptedBinding` event is emitted on the RFQ update stream. A binding accepted RFQ cannot be cancelled by the requester. - Settlement completes shortly afterwards, once the broker has executed the offsetting transaction. The fill is emitted as an `rfqFilled` event and appears in the RFQ fill history. Settlement may occur at the quoted price or at a better price. - If the quote is not settled within the settlement window, the RFQ is cancelled by the system and the locked funds are released. - The RFQ, quote, and fill history endpoints accept a `deferredSettlement` parameter to filter deferred settlement activity. Third-party makers can quote stock market RFQs through the public API (`POST /api/v1/rfq/quote`) if they hold the inventory to deliver: quotes submitted through the API always settle immediately on acceptance. Deferred settlement quoting — where acceptance is binding and settlement follows — is used by the exchange broker and is not available over the public API.

--- # Infrastructure Orders are processed through a single linear command stream. All orders from all API instances feed into one stream, which is consumed by the matching engine sequentially. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Client["Client"] direction LR REST["REST API Client"] WSC["WebSocket Client"] end subgraph Edge["Edge"] direction LR WAF["WAF"] CDN["CDN"] end ALB["Load Balancer"] API["API
N pods, Pre-validation"] BUS["Message Bus"] subgraph Engine["Matching Engine"] direction LR CLEARING["Clearing"] OB["Order Book"] SETTLE["Settlement"] end WSLB["WebSocket LB"] APIWS["WebSocket API
N pods"] subgraph Persistence["Persistence"] direction LR DB["Database"] SNAP["Snapshots"] end REST <-->|"Order / Execution Response"| WAF WAF <--> CDN CDN <--> ALB ALB <--> API API <--> BUS BUS <--> Engine CLEARING --> OB OB --> SETTLE Engine --> WSLB WSLB --> APIWS APIWS -->|"Order Updates / Depth / Trades"| WSC Engine -.-> Persistence classDef hotpath fill:#ff6b6b,stroke:#c0392b,color:#fff classDef bus fill:#f39c12,stroke:#e67e22,color:#fff classDef client fill:#3498db,stroke:#2980b9,color:#fff classDef persist fill:#95a5a6,stroke:#7f8c8d,color:#fff classDef edge fill:#1abc9c,stroke:#16a085,color:#fff class REST,WSC client class WAF,CDN,ALB,WSLB edge class API,APIWS,CLEARING,OB,SETTLE hotpath class BUS bus class DB,SNAP persist ``` ## Order Lifecycle ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '12px'}}}%% sequenceDiagram participant Client as Client participant API as API participant Engine as Matching Engine participant WS as WebSocket API Client->>+API: POST /api/v1/order (signed) API->>+Engine: Order command Note over Engine: Clear → Match → Settle Engine-->>-API: Execution response API->>-Client: HTTP 200 — Order result Engine->>WS: Engine events WS->>Client: Order updates / Depth / Trades ``` ## Taker Speed Bump A speed bump (currently 100ms) is applied to all taker (non-post-only) orders across all spot and futures markets. It is designed to reinforce top-of-book liquidity by protecting resting orders from latency-driven adverse selection. - The speed bump applies to any order submitted without the `postOnly` flag — market orders and limit orders (including IOC), even if the order ultimately rests on the order book. - Orders with `postOnly` enabled are not subject to the speed bump. - Order cancellations are exempt and are processed without delay. - The speed bump applies uniformly to all participants.

--- # Changelog ## 2026-10-02 - Add `GET /api/v1/stockIndicativeQuote`. It returns the price that the stock quoter quotes now on an RFQ for a stock, side and quantity, or the reason that no quote is available. It needs no account and no balance. The price is a limit price: the RFQ settles at this price or better. - Add the `stockIndicativeQuote.` WebSocket stream. It pushes the same quotes for both sides once per second and uses bare stock tickers, like `stockPrice.`. - Add an estimated price to stock indicative quotes: `estimatedPrice` on `GET /api/v1/stockIndicativeQuote`, and `estimatedBid`/`estimatedAsk` on `stockIndicativeQuote.`. It is the settle price when the quoter hedges at the current market bid or ask. The fill can be better or worse than the estimate, but never worse than the limit price. - Rename `GET /api/v1/market-sessions` to `GET /api/v1/stockSessions` and `GET /api/v1/market-holidays` to `GET /api/v1/stockHolidays`. The old paths still work but are deprecated. ## 2026-08-03 - The WebSocket API now supports `permessage-deflate` compression (RFC 7692). Clients that offer the extension during the handshake receive compressed frames; clients that do not offer it are unaffected. Enabling it substantially reduces bandwidth on high-volume streams such as `depth.` and `bookTicker.` — most WebSocket libraries support it via a client option (browsers and Python `websockets` enable it by default). - Add the `stockPrice.` WebSocket stream for provider-derived stock quotes. It uses bare stock tickers and includes bid, ask, mid, source timestamp, and trading session fields. ## 2026-08-01 - Add the `account.balanceUpdate` WebSocket stream. Whenever the balance of an asset in the account changes, the new absolute available, locked and staked quantities for that asset are pushed to this private stream. ## 2026-07-23 - Add the `externalTicker.` WebSocket stream for provider-derived 24-hour ticker statistics. The existing `ticker.` stream remains venue-only. ## 2026-07-17 - Removed `CulledBorrowInterest`, `CulledRealizePnl`, and `CulledRealizePnlBookUtilization` settlement source filters. Culled realize PnL settlements are now reported as `RealizePnl`. Culled borrow interest settlements are now reported as `TradingFees`. ## 2026-07-11 - Document stock trading. Tokenized stocks trade through the RFQ flow during market sessions, and through the spot order book outside of market hours for listed stocks — see the new Stock Trading section. - Add the RFQ instruction types to the list of valid signing instructions in the Authentication section. The instructions themselves are unchanged and were already documented on each RFQ endpoint. - Correct several RFQ documentation inaccuracies: quotes must be submitted before the RFQ submission time (not the expiry time); only the current best quote for an RFQ can be accepted; refreshing an RFQ cancels its existing quotes; document the `Expired` status and the maker-side fields on the `rfqAcceptedBinding` and `rfqFilled` stream events. ## 2025-11-12 - Backstop liquidation fills now include a non-zero `tradeId` field on an on-going basis. Previously such fills had a zero `tradeId`. This applies to the `/fills` endpoint as well as the trade stream. ## 2025-11-10 - Add a specific error message for withdrawal attempts to non-2FA exempt withdrawal addresses. - Set a default limit of `1000` levels each side of the book for `/depth` endpoint. ## 2025-10-23 - Add `j` and `k` fields to the order update stream (take profit limit price and stop loss limit price). ## 2025-09-02 - The `/depth` endpoint now returns a limit of 5,000 price levels on each side of the book. ## 2025-09-01 - The `cumulativeInterest` response field is being removed from the `/position`endpoint. - Estimated liquidation price or `l` is being removed from the position update stream. It will remain as a placeholder and be set to 0. It will be removed in the future, so client's should not rely on its presence. - Liquidation price can be queried for a single position using the Positions API `/position` for example `/position?symbol=BTC_USDC_PERP`. ## 2025-08-07 - `/history/pnl` has been removed. ## 2025-06-08 - The order id format is changing, it is no longer a byte shifted timestamp. It is no longer possible to derive the order timestamp from the order id. This change will take place at Monday June 9th, 01:00 UTC. ## 2025-04-22 - The `/fills` endpoint now returns all fills for the account, including fills from system orders as well as client orders. System orders include liquidations, ADLs and collateral conversions. Previously, by default, it only returned fills from client orders. This behavior can be achieved by setting the `fillType` parameter to `User`. ## 2025-04-08 - Added funding rate lower and upper bounds to `/markets` and `/market` endpoints. ## 2025-03-26 - Add open interest stream `openInterest.`. - Added the option to query `/history/borrowLend/positions` with a signed request using the instruction `borrowPositionHistoryQueryAll`. ## 2025-03-19 - The leverage filter has been removed from `/markets` and `/market` endpoints. - Added `/openInterest` now takes `symbol` as an optional parameter. When not set, all markets are returned. - `/openInterests` has been deprecated. - Add stop loss and take profit fields to `/orders/execute`. - Add `I` field to the order update stream (related order id). - Add `a` and `b` fields to the order update stream (take profit trigger price and stop loss trigger price). ## 2025-02-28 - Added `clientId` to fill history. ## 2025-02-11 - An `O` field has been added to the order update stream. It denotes the origin of the update. The possible values are: - `USER`: The origin of the update was due to order entry by the user. - `LIQUIDATION_AUTOCLOSE`: The origin of the update was due to a liquidation by the liquidation engine. - `ADL_AUTOCLOSE`: The origin of the update was due to an ADL (auto-deleveraging) event. - `COLLATERAL_CONVERSION`: The origin of the update was due to a collateral conversion to settle debt on the account. - `SETTLEMENT_AUTOCLOSE`: The origin of the update was due to the settlement of a position on a dated market. - `BACKSTOP_LIQUIDITY_PROVIDER`: The origin of the update was due to a backstop liquidity provider facilitating a liquidation. ## 2025-02-07 - Added `r` to denote a reduce only order on the order updates stream. - Added `reduceOnly` to the get orders endpoint. ## 2025-02-03 - Added `openInterestLimit` to the markets endpoint. Applicable to futures markets only. - Added `orderModified` event to the order update stream. A resting reduce only order's quantity can be decreased in order to prevent position side reversal. ## 2025-01-09 - Added `marketType` to the markets endpoint. - Added an optional `marketType` filter to the fills and the orders endpoints. ## 2024-12-03 - Add order expiry reason to order update stream. - Add `cumulativeInterest` to borrow lend position. ## 2024-12-02 - Add borrow lend history per position endpoint. ## 2024-11-10 - Add `timestamp` field denoting the system time in unix-epoch microseconds to the depth endpoint. ## 2024-10-15 - Convert all error responses to JSON and add a error code. ## 2024-05-14 - Add `executedQuantity` and `executedQuoteQuantity` to order history endpoint. ## 2024-05-03 - Add single market order update stream `account.orderUpdate.`. ## 2024-05-02 - Add optional `from` and `to` timestamp to get withdrawals endpoint. ## 2024-05-01 - Add optional `from` and `to` timestamp to get deposits endpoint. ## 2024-03-14 - Add optional `orderId` filter to order history endpoint. - Add optional `from` and `to` timestamp to order fills endpoint. ## 2024-02-28 - Return the withdrawal in request withdrawal response. ## 2024-02-24 - An additional field `t` was added to the private order update stream. It is the `trade_id` of the fill that generated the order update. - Added a maximum value for the `X-Window` header of `60000`. ## 2024-01-16 ### Breaking - A new websocket API is available at `wss://ws.backpack.exchange`. Please see the documentation. The previous API remains on the same endpoint and will be deprecated after a migration period. The new API changes the following: - Subscription endpoint is now `wss://ws.backpack.exchange` instead of `wss://ws.backpack.exchange/stream`. - Can subscribe and unsubscribe to/from multiple streams by passing more than one in the `params` field. - Signature should now be sent in a separate `signature` field. - Signature instruction changed from `accountQuery` to `subscribe`. - Event and engine timestamps are now in `microseconds` instead of `milliseconds`. - Add engine timestamp to `bookTicker`, `depth`, and `order` streams. - Add quote asset volume to ticker stream. - Add sequential trade id to trade stream. - Rename the event type in the depth stream from `depthEvent` to `depth`. - Change the format of streams from `@` to `.` or `kline..` for K-lines. - Flatten the K-Line in the K-line stream so its not nested. ## 2024-01-11 ### Breaking - Replaced `identifier` field on deposits with `transaction_hash` and `provider_id`. This aims to provide clearer representation of the field, particularly for fiat deposits. - Removed duplicate `pending` values from the `WithdrawalStatus` and `DepositStatus` spec enum.

get.description:
Retrieves an open order from the order book. This only returns the order
if it is resting on the order book (i.e. has not been completely filled,
expired, or cancelled).

One of `orderId` or `clientId` must be specified; provide only one.
If both are provided, `orderId` takes precedence and signed requests
fail signature verification.

**Instruction:** `orderQuery`

autoBorrowSettlements.description: If true, then tries to borrow during collateral reconciliation.

autoLend.description: If true, then tries to automatically lend with available balance.

autoRealizePnl.description: Determines if the account should have continuous PnL realization.

autoRepayBorrows.description:
If true, then tries to automatically repay borrows with available
balance.

futuresMakerFee.description: Futures maker fee in basis points. Negative if a rebate exists.

futuresTakerFee.description: Futures taker fee in basis points.

spotMakerFee.description: Spot maker fee in basis points. Negative if a rebate exists.

spotTakerFee.description: Spot taker fee in basis points.

AssetClass.description:
Market asset-class filter. `Stock` matches markets involving a
tokenized-stock asset; `Crypto` matches everything else.

locked.description:
Funds that are locked because they are in an order that has not been
executed.

totalQuantity.description: Pre haircut quantity of the asset.

balanceNotional.description:
Balance of spot instrument in USDC.
This is calculated as `index_price * balance`.

collateralWeight.description: Collateral weight of spot instrument, applied as a haircut.

collateralValue.description:
Collateral Value (or adjusted equity).
This is calculated as `index_price * balance * collateral_weight`.

openOrderQuantity.description: The amount added to collateral from open orders.

lendQuantity.description: The amount added to collateral from lending.

availableQuantity.description: The amount of freely available assets.

symbol.description: The symbol of the market associated to the funding interval.

intervalEndTimestamp.description: The end of the funding interval.

fundingRate.description: The funding rate for the interval.

userId.description: User id of the account the payment is associated with.

subaccountId.description: Id of the subaccount the payment is associated with, if any.

symbol.description: The symbol of the market the payment is associated with.

quantity.description: Quantity of the payment. Positive if received, negative if paid.

intervalEndTimestamp.description: The end of the funding interval for the payment.

fundingRate.description: The funding rate for the payment.

estLiquidationPrice.description: Estimated liquidation price for this position.

imf.description: Initial margin fraction for this position.

allOf.description: IMF function.

markPrice.description: Mark price for this position's market.

mmf.description: Maintenance margin fraction for this position.

allOf.description: MMF function.

netCost.description:
Positive if long. Negative if short.

The net cost to enter into the position,i.e., price*quantity for
all positions adjusting this position.

netQuantity.description: Positive if long. Negative if short.

netExposureQuantity.description: Quantity of this futures position including worst case open positions.

netExposureNotional.description:
Notional value of the futures position including worst case open
positions.

pnlRealized.description: Aggregates the amount of pnl realized on this position since opening.

pnlUnrealized.description: Unrealized profit and loss for this position.

cumulativeFundingPayment.description: Cumulative funding payment for this position.

subaccountId.description: ID of the user subaccount that the position is for.

symbol.description: Future to which this position belongs.

cumulativeInterest.description: Cumulative interest paid for this position's unrealized pnl.

executedQuoteQuantity.description: The quantity of the quote asset that has been filled.

postOnly.description: Whether the order is post only or not

price.description:
The limit price. The order book will only match this order with
other orders at this price or better.

reduceOnly.description: True if reducing a futures position.

selfTradePrevention.description:
Action to take in the event the user crosses themselves in the
order book. Default is `RejectTaker`.

allOf.description:
Action to take in the event the user crosses themselves in the
order book. Default is `RejectTaker`.
Status of the order.

Stop loss limit price. If set the stop loss will be a limit order,
otherwise it will be a market order.

Take profit limit price. If set the take profit will be a limit order,
otherwise it will be a market order.
